precepts.text: The people clave to their nobles and entered into a curse and an oath to walk in God's law given by Moses and to do all his commandments.
precepts.point: This flows out of the covenant made in chapter 10, where the people entered into a curse and an oath to walk in the law of Moses, keep the Sabbath, and not marry the people of the land. Coming back into the land, they began to apply the things they had always done.
precepts.why:
The rulers dwelt at Jerusalem and the people cast lots to bring one of ten to dwell in the holy city. This flows out of the covenant made in chapter 10: “They clave to their brethren, their nobles, and entered into a curse, and into an oath, to walk in God’s law, which was given by Moses the servant of God, and to observe and do all the commandments of the Lord our Lord, and his judgments and his statutes”.

The people clave to their nobles and bound themselves by a curse and an oath to walk in the law given by Moses and do all his commandments. Coming back into the land, they began to apply the things they had always done, and filling the holy city again is part of that.

precepts.text: Part of that oath was that they would not give their daughters to the people of the land nor take their daughters for their sons.
precepts.point: This flows out of the covenant made in chapter 10, where the people entered into a curse and an oath to walk in the law of Moses, keep the Sabbath, and not marry the people of the land. Coming back into the land, they began to apply the things they had always done.
precepts.why:
Part of the oath the people entered into was this: “And that we would not give our daughters unto the people of the land, nor take their daughters for our sons”.

They swore not to marry the people of the land. This is one of the things they had always been commanded, and as they came back into the land and repopulated Jerusalem they began to apply it again.

precepts.text: They also swore not to buy victuals from the people of the land on the Sabbath day, the same Sabbath commerce Nehemiah later has to enforce in chapter 13.
precepts.point: This flows out of the covenant made in chapter 10, where the people entered into a curse and an oath to walk in the law of Moses, keep the Sabbath, and not marry the people of the land. Coming back into the land, they began to apply the things they had always done.
precepts.why:
They also swore about the Sabbath: “And if the people of the land bring ware or any victuals on the sabbath day to sell, that we would not buy it of them on the sabbath, or on the holy day: and that we would leave the seventh year, and the exaction of every debt.”

Not buying victuals from the people of the land on the Sabbath day is the same Sabbath commerce Nehemiah later has to enforce in chapter 13. The oath was made in chapter 10, the city was filled in chapter 11, and keeping the Sabbath in that city was part of what they had sworn to do.

precepts.text: As the holy city is filled again, the haughtiness of the daughters of Zion is a warning against pride and outward vanity in the restored people.
precepts.point: This flows out of the covenant made in chapter 10, where the people entered into a curse and an oath to walk in the law of Moses, keep the Sabbath, and not marry the people of the land. Coming back into the land, they began to apply the things they had always done.
precepts.why:
As the holy city is filled again, Isaiah's word stands as a warning: “Because the daughters of Zion are haughty, and walk with stretched forth necks and wanton eyes, walking and mincing as they go, and making a tinkling with their feet: Therefore the Lord will smite with a scab the crown of the head of the daughters of Zion, and the Lord will discover their secret parts.”

The haughtiness of the daughters of Zion, the stretched forth necks, wanton eyes and tinkling feet, brought judgment on Jerusalem before. For the restored people dwelling in the holy city, it is a warning against pride and outward vanity.

precepts.text: A certain portion for the singers due for every day was set by the king's commandment, showing that even under a foreign king the temple service was provided for.
precepts.point: The porters that kept the gates are numbered, and the Nethinims dwelt in Ophel. The singers were over the business of the house of God, for it was the king's commandment that a certain portion should be for the singers due for every day.
precepts.why:
Among the Levites, the sons of Asaph, the singers, were over the business of the house of God, and their portion was provided: “For it was the king’s commandment concerning them, that a certain portion should be for the singers, due for every day.”

A certain portion for the singers, due every day, was set by the king's commandment. Even under a foreign king the temple service was provided for. The Levites had oversight of the outward business of the house of God, Mattaniah began the thanksgiving in prayer, the porters kept the gates, and the singers had their daily portion by the king's own word.

points: The rulers of the people dwelt at Jerusalem, and the rest of the people cast lots to bring one of ten to dwell in the holy city, while nine parts remained in the other cities.
These verses name the children of Judah and Benjamin who dwelt in Jerusalem: from Judah, Athaiah of the line of Perez, and Maaseiah of the line of Shiloni; from Benjamin, Sallu and his brethren.

Four hundred threescore and eight valiant men of the sons of Perez dwelt in Jerusalem, and Joel and Judah were set as overseers over the city. These are a name register, the record of the families that repopulated the city.
These verses name the priests: Jedaiah, Jachin, and Seraiah, who was the ruler of the house of God, with their brethren that did the work of the house numbering eight hundred twenty and two.
More priests are named after them, with their chief men, and their overseer was Zabdiel, one of the great men. This is the register of the priesthood that served in the holy city.

These verses name the Levites and their duties: Shemaiah and others, and the chief Levites who had oversight of the outward business of the house of God, and Mattaniah who was the principal to begin the thanksgiving in prayer.

The porters that kept the gates are numbered, and the Nethinims dwelt in Ophel. The singers were over the business of the house of God, for it was the king's commandment that a certain portion should be for the singers due for every day.

These verses list the villages where the children of Judah dwelt, from Kirjatharba to Beersheba and its valleys, and where the children of Benjamin dwelt, from Geba to Michmash and the surrounding towns.
Certain divisions of the Levites in Judah were joined to Benjamin. This closes the register of where the returned people settled across the land, each in his inheritance.
